Subject: Deal structure override request: Veridian Health Q4 pilot

Team —

Quick summary: Veridian Health (regional provider network) wants to convert a proof-of-concept into a Q4 pilot. They are asking for a one-time 40% platform discount for the first 6 months and a capped per-token rate thereafter. Their legal has pushed back on standard usage SLAs and wants a 24-month minimum commitment written into the SOW.

Why I think we should consider an exception:
- They agree to a 24-month minimum with a $1.2M committed spend floor (we'd capture in SOW).
- High strategic value: three regional hospitals in their network are likely to convert after pilot (sales estimate 60% conversion).
- They will be a reference customer for our HIPAA Private deployment.

Request: I need executive approval (VP/CFO) to approve a 40% starter discount for months 1–6, and to allow seat-based surcharges to be negotiated post-pilot. If not, the customer requests we return to standard 25% starter discount + extended onboarding credits — they may pause timelines.

Attachments: Veridian_SOW_v1.pdf; veridian_pricing_workbook.xlsx (proposed pricing vs our guardrails).

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick margin calc and runway impact for CFO (Aditya) — see workbook.
2) If acceptable, Marissa to sign off commercial exception and Jordan to confirm contract path.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call.

—Kimberly

Kimberly —

Thanks for the concise summary. A few quick asks before I greenlight anything:
- Aditya: can you run a 24-month NPV and gross margin for the proposed 40% starter discount vs our standard 25%? Include any expected uplift from seat add-ons and the projected conversion (Kim's 60% estimate).
- Kimberly: send me the procurement redlines (they mentioned SLA edits) so Legal/Contracts can scope changes.
- What is the requested effective date for the discount and the trigger for the post-pilot pricing?

My initial view: a 40% starter discount is above our usual guardrail for this segment. If the economics look favorable (net margin > 35% over two years with the commitment floor), I'll consider a conditional approval. If not, we should offer a phased discount: 30% for months 1–3, 20% months 4–6, and a guaranteed floor on committed spend to protect revenue.

Please push the procurement redlines and the customer's confirmation of the $1.2M minimum into this thread. I'll review once Aditya posts the numbers.

—Marissa

Team —

I ran the numbers off the workbook Kimberly provided. High level:
- 24-month committed revenue: $1.2M baseline (from customer floor) + expected overage if conversion materializes (we conservatively model +20% uplift in year 2).
- With a 40% starter discount for months 1–6, blended gross margin over 24 months results in ~38% (below our preferred 40% target but defensible given reference value and strategic placement in the northeast market).
- If we implement a phased approach (30% months 1–3, 20% months 4–6), margin improves to ~43% and reduces downside risk.

Conditional approval: I will sign off on an exception to allow up to 40% starter discount provided all of the following are met:
1) Legal provides an addendum that limits SLA financial exposure (cap on credits at X% of monthly charges) and includes audit-log retention language acceptable to Security.
2) Jordan confirms contract path and that the SOW records the $1.2M minimum and an overage calculation.
3) Commercial commits to a phased discount if Legal cannot negotiate the protections above (30/20 as fallback).

Jordan — please evaluate contract risk and advise on the addendum language. Marissa — if you agree with the conditional constraints, Kimberly can present the package to the customer with these guardrails.

—Aditya
